intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14), a lower motor neuron disease, is caused by mutation in the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin (DCTN1) on chromosome 2p13.

checks.claim: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is a lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the disorder a lower motor neuron disease. It does not use the name 'distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14' or the symbol HMND14.

checks.claim: HMND14 is caused by mutation in the DCTN1 gene, which encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a mutation in the gene for dynactin's largest subunit (DCTN1) in this disease and concludes that dynactin dysfunction can cause it.

checks.claim: The DCTN1 gene is located on chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13. Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The gene lies in the linked interval at 2p13.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is a lower motor neuron disease. It has been associated with a missense mutation in the largest subunit of dynactin, a protein involved in axonal transport, and with reduced binding of the mutant protein to microtubules (Puls et al., 2003).

checks.claim: Distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-14 (HMND14) is a lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the disorder a lower motor neuron disease. The HMND14 name and symbol are not in the paper.

checks.claim: HMND14 has been associated with a missense mutation in the largest subunit of dynactin, a protein involved in axonal transport.
checks.evidence_quote: a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: A single base-pair change that causes an amino acid substitution is a missense mutation.

checks.claim: HMND14 has been associated with reduced binding of the mutant dynactin protein to microtubules.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) studied a family with lower motor neuron disease. The abstract-level evidence does not give the number of affected members or their detailed clinical findings.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) studied a family with lower motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a lower motor neuron disease. Linkage analysis implies family data, but the abstract never says that a single family was studied.

paragraphs.text: In a family with lower motor neuron disease, Puls et al. (2003) found linkage of the disorder to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.

checks.claim: In a family with lower motor neuron disease, Puls et al. (2003) found linkage of the disorder to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.
checks.explanation: The linkage to a 4-Mb region at 2p13 is stated. The abstract does not say this was found in one family.

paragraphs.text: In the affected members of a family with lower motor neuron disease linked to chromosome 2p13, Puls et al. (2003) analyzed a gene in the linked interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin. They found a single base-pair change resulting in an amino acid substitution. They predicted that the substitution would distort the folding of the microtubule-binding domain of dynactin. In binding assays, the mutant dynactin protein bound less to microtubules.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) analyzed the gene encoding the largest subunit of dynactin, located in the linked interval, in affected members of a family with lower motor neuron disease linked to chromosome 2p13.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin
checks.explanation: The gene analysis is stated. The abstract does not say that a family or its affected members were studied; that detail is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the affected members of the family with lower motor neuron disease linked to 2p13, Puls et al. (2003) found a single base-pair change in the dynactin large-subunit gene that results in an amino acid substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution
checks.explanation: The single base-pair change and resulting substitution are stated. The abstract does not say it was found in a family's affected members.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) predicted that the dynactin amino acid substitution would distort the folding of the microtubule-binding domain of dynactin.
checks.evidence_quote: an amino-acid substitution that is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain

checks.claim: In binding assays, the mutant dynactin protein from the lower motor neuron disease family bound less to microtubules.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.

paragraphs.text: Puls et al. (2003) found that mutant dynactin bound less to microtubules in binding assays. They concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated axonal transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) found that mutant dynactin bound less to microtubules in binding assays.
checks.evidence_quote: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.

checks.claim: Puls et al. (2003) concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated axonal transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract. The draft's word 'axonal' fits the abstract's description of dynactin as an axonal transport protein.
